title: Compiler-independent Typert type model
summary: The Typert generator uses the TypeScript compiler only to extract types, then works from its own compiler-independent model of packages, services, events and types when it emits runtime schemas and reflection data.
firstReason: TypeScript tooling: the generator exists because TypeScript types are erased at run time. Go types are available at run time through reflection and at build time through the standard go/types packages, so there is no separate type model to design.

title: One Remote failure vocabulary for ctx.remote
summary: All remote calls report failure through one error type that carries a code and typed details; domains no longer define their own error families and mapping functions.
firstReason: One coded error type across the API boundary is simple to keep in Go and serves the JSON-RPC protocol used by SDKs and plugin processes.

title: Unified Typert/Remote metadata
summary: Proposed, not built: generate one ordinary metadata artifact per Remote method (description, named-input parser, JSON Schema, result metadata) so that CLI help, argument parsing and MCP tool discovery work offline, with input strictness chosen by the consumer.
firstReason: Adopt the goal, not the mechanism. A single description of each API method that feeds CLI help, MCP tool schemas and SDK types is valuable in Go too; Typert's TypeScript analysis and its two compiler programs are not available. Inference: the Go API spec should define methods once as Go descriptors and generate the rest.

title: SDK native user questions
summary: SDK clients (TypeScript and Python) may register a question callback and advertise it at initialization. The SDK server then routes the `ask_user_question` interaction to the client over a bidirectional call for the root agents it owns, validates a complete batch of answers and cancels pending questions when the tool or server stops.
firstReason: An out-of-process host must be able to answer questions, or the tool has no answerer. The Python SDK is in scope (DH-ADR-1); the wire details may change (DH-ADR-2), but the capability handshake and the cancellation rules should stay.

title: ACP as an automation-only protocol
summary: The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) bridge is an automation transport only: sessions, one prompt at a time, model configuration, MCP mounting, committed updates, cancellation and one-shot permission requests. It no longer renders editor cards, pickers or other presentation.
firstReason: Keeping presentation out of an automation transport prevents a third user interface from growing beside the web UI and the terminal. The scope decision is independent of the language.
